Snapline 2.14.0

  • Your camera joins screen recordings: turn on Camera in the Record Screen bar and your webcam floats over the capture as a bubble that's filmed right into the movie. Drag it anywhere, resize it by the badge on its outline, pick circle or rectangle, and style its border — presets, gradients, glow — from the bar or the new Settings → Recording tab.
  • A tidier Record Screen bar: the microphone picker and the camera's controls appear only while their toggle is on, instead of sitting dimmed.
  • Recording robustness: pausing no longer cuts the last frames before the pause, and a recording stopped the instant it starts no longer leaves the screen-recording indicator lit. A camera lost mid-take fades out and says so; the recording continues.
  • Scrolling capture's finish message stays current instead of going stale, a plain click on an annotation no longer wipes redo history, and the capture card's save dialog no longer lets the card slide away underneath it.

Snapline 2.13.0

The text tool becomes a real text box, and the Screen Recording permission flow gets untangled — one dialog at a time, and it's the right one.

Annotate

  • The text tool becomes a real text box. Drag to place a text box at the width you want — text wraps inside it instead of running in one line. Move it by its border, resize it from either side handle, scale it from the corner, and restyle it live from the color and size pickers while you type.
  • Editing that behaves like editing. Enter types a newline; ⌘-Enter or a click outside commits; Esc keeps a non-empty draft; ⌘Z steps back through your typing. What you see while typing is exactly what commits — no shift when the draft lands.
  • Click to re-edit. With the text tool active, clicking an existing text box opens it for editing instead of stacking a new one on top. Text from earlier versions keeps its old auto-width look until you edit it.

Permissions

  • No more stacked dialogs. When Screen Recording access is missing, macOS's own prompt now goes first — Snapline stays quiet behind it instead of piling its own alert on top.
  • The Settings button lands somewhere useful. Snapline's alert now registers the app with macOS before opening System Settings, so the Screen Recording list always has a Snapline row to act on.
  • Honest instructions. The alert no longer blames "the update" for a missing grant, and its steps cover both cases: a stale entry that needs removing and re-adding, and no entry at all.
  • Relaunch offered, not homework. Once you grant access, Snapline notices and offers to relaunch itself so recording features pick up the permission.
  • No more dead shortcut. A capture attempt after a declined prompt now explains the way forward instead of silently doing nothing.

Snapline 2.12.0

Screen recordings can carry sound: your microphone, what your Mac is playing, or both — each its own track in the movie.

New

  • Microphone and System Audio for recordings. Two toggles, in Settings → General and right on the Record Screen bar. Each source is written as its own track, never mixed, so an editor can pull either apart later. Both are off by default — a recording stays silent until you say otherwise.
  • Pick your microphone. The Record Screen bar lists every connected input. Your choice sticks; if the device isn't connected at record time, Snapline says so, records with the system default, and shows the missing device as "not connected" until you re-pick.

Notes

  • A recording never fails because of the microphone. Access refused, no input device, or a microphone unplugged mid-take — Snapline tells you at the time, and the video (and any system audio) is exactly what it would have been.
  • Audio stays in step with the picture through pauses, stalls, and long takes — gaps are healed rather than letting the soundtrack drift.
  • Snapline's own notification pills no longer appear in recordings.
  • Recorded audio stays inside the movie file on your Mac; nothing is uploaded. Snapline asks for microphone access only when you turn Microphone on — the privacy policy spells it out.
